items.hed: The Houston Rockets, fresh off back-to-back wins over the Clippers and Suns at Toyota Center, host the Philadelphia 76ers tonight at 8:30 p.m. ET — their first game since Wednesday's 116-104 win over Phoenix
items.insight: NBA.com's official 2026-27 schedule, re-checked same-turn this morning, confirms tonight's 8:30 p.m. ET tip-off against Philadelphia at Toyota Center is the Rockets' next game, with no game played since the Nov. 25 win over the Suns. The Rockets have won five of their last six and sit on a run that includes wins over the Clippers (Nov. 23) and Suns (Nov. 25), both at home. No injury report or starting lineup for tonight was posted on the team's own schedule page as of this morning's check; this item will carry forward to tonight's board once the game is played.

items.hed: The Texans' final Week 12 injury report before Sunday's home game against Baltimore shows four players ruled out — wide receiver Kayshon Boutte, edge rusher Danielle Hunter, tight end Brevin Jordan and lineman Keylan Rutledge — unchanged from Friday's report
items.insight: The Texans' own injury-report page, re-checked same-turn this morning, still shows Boutte (hip), Hunter (hamstring), Jordan (finger/foot) and Rutledge (neck/shoulder) all listed OUT after sitting out practice all week — this is Friday's final report and the last update expected before Sunday's kickoff at NRG Stadium. Linebacker Jacob Hummel (abdomen/groin) remains Questionable after progressing to full practice Friday. Defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins (ankle) and tight end Dalton Schultz (illness) both carry no game-status designation after reaching full participation Friday. No new names were added to the report since yesterday afternoon's check.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium (formerly Reliant Stadium), Houston. Venue still.

items.hed: New Astros general manager Randy Flores' reshaping of a Houston outfield that posted the majors' second-worst OPS last season remains at the same stage it was yesterday — outrighting Joey Loperfido and non-tendering Taylor Trammell, with the bigger additions still to come
items.insight: MLB.com's Astros news page, re-checked same-turn this morning, shows no new Astros-specific transaction since yesterday's board; the top entries are league-wide pieces (a 2026 season statistical recap, a Hot Stove trade-pace note) rather than Astros news. The club's last reported moves remain outrighting Loperfido and non-tendering Trammell to clear outfield roster space, following new manager Brad Ausmus' hires of J.P. Martinez at pitching coach and Aaron Bates at hitting coach. The outfield posted a .662 OPS last season, 29th of 30 teams, which Flores is now working to address.
